source.title: The hippocampus supports multiple cognitive processes through relational binding and comparison.

confidence_rationale: A review whose thesis is, almost verbatim, MECH-044: the hippocampus rapidly, continuously and obligatorily forms associations among disparate elements across space and time AND enables comparison of stored representations against current input -- i.e. relational binding AND comparison, extending beyond long-term storage into ongoing cognition. The mapping to MECH-044 is the tightest in this pull. Held below the top band because it is a review (synthesis of eye-movement, amnesia, and fMRI evidence) rather than a single decisive experiment, and because 'continuous/obligatory online binding' is the strong end of the literature -- a falsifiable but not universally settled position.
failure_signatures: The 'obligatory, continuous, online' framing is the strong end of the hippocampal-function debate; conjunctive-coding and pure long-term-consolidation accounts contest whether binding/comparison is genuinely ONLINE or a retrieval artifact -- a REE design that wires hippocampal binding into the moment-to-moment loop adopts the contested strong reading.

The review aggregates human eye-movement, developmental-amnesia and fMRI evidence; it does not by itself isolate the binding-vs-comparison computations mechanistically, so it grounds THAT the hippocampus does relational binding+comparison, not a circuit-level HOW that REE could copy.

Relational binding here is across arbitrary elements (faces, scenes, items); it is not specifically about OBJECT-file token persistence, so it supports MECH-044 strongly but only indirectly supports the object-file clause of ARC-006/MECH-045.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The hippocampus's critical role is to rapidly, continuously and obligatorily bind disparate elements across space and time and to compare internal representations against current perceptual input; this binding-and-comparison function reaches far beyond explicit long-term recognition memory into many ongoing cognitive operations.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-044 asserts 'hippocampal systems participate in relational binding and comparison, not only long-term storage', supporting early detection of relations and binding consistency across time and context. Olsen et al. is the direct biological grounding: it is the review that establishes relational binding AND comparison as a general, online hippocampal computation rather than a storage-only role -- exactly MECH-044's distinction. It also supports ARC-006's constraint that 'relational binding is first-class' and 'hippocampal systems may participate early in relational binding/comparison rather than only in long-term storage.'
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review establishes the functional role at the systems level from human eye-movement/amnesia/fMRI evidence; it does not give a circuit-level mechanism REE can copy, and the 'obligatory online' reading is the strong (contested) end of the debate. Binding here is over arbitrary relational elements, not specifically object-file token persistence.
mapping.source_context: Review/synthesis; human eye-movement (relational manipulation index), developmental and adult amnesia, and fMRI studies of hippocampal binding and comparison.

confidence_components.notes: Very high mapping fidelity -- MECH-044's wording tracks this review's thesis. source_quality moderate-high (authoritative review, not a single decisive study); transfer_risk modest (human-to-agent, plus adopting the strong online-binding reading).
